what: The ICTV family of each genome in `data/benchmark_panel.json`, so a panel-wide aggregate can state an independent unit instead of assuming one.
why: benchmarks/README.md records the defect this answers: '26 of 46 genomes sit in a pattern-identical group. Five coronaviruses share one pattern list; five biologically unrelated viruses share RdRp / Glycoprotein / Nucleoprotein. Only ~20 rows have a unique list, so an aggregate over 46 independent instances is inflated. Combine within family first, then across families.' Recall@k over 47 genomes treats five coronaviruses as five draws when the ranker identifies all five through the same curated relatives and scores them on the same target names; they are closer to one draw than to five. The holdout makes each genome name its proteins through a relative, and within a family the relative is usually another member of the panel's own family group, which is exactly the dependence a per-genome mean ignores.
assignment_rule: ICTV family as of the 2024 release, taken from the NCBI Taxonomy lineage of each accession's own organism. Two renames matter and are used in their current form: the five herpesviruses are Orthoherpesviridae (formerly Herpesviridae), and the three bunyavirus-order segmented genomes are separated into Hantaviridae, Nairoviridae and Phenuiviridae rather than pooled as 'Bunyaviridae', which no longer exists. Pooling them would have made one unit of three unrelated viruses and understated the denominator in the opposite direction.
note_on_singletons: Eleven of the 21 families carry exactly one genome, so a family-combined mean is not a variance reduction -- it is a re-weighting. A singleton family keeps its genome's full weight while each of the eight Flaviviridae keeps an eighth of one. That is the point: the inflation being corrected is that the panel's largest families are also its best-curated ones.
note_on_unscoreable: Human parvovirus B19 (NC_000883.2) returns 8 ORFs and zero identified chains, so it has no ranking to score and is the sole member of Parvoviridae. A family whose only genome is unscoreable drops out of the aggregate rather than counting as a zero, which is the same rule the panel's own `unscoreable_note` states for the genome.
